answers.q1: `matchEntityRegExp = /&(?:quot|amp|lt|gt|#([0-9]+)|#[xX]([0-9a-fA-F]+));/g`. It is case-sensitive and requires the trailing `;`.
answers.q2: The function is named `unescapeHtml`. It is exported as `module.exports.unescape = unescapeHtml`, a property on the existing `escapeHtml` export.
answers.q3: `'` matches the regex's decimal numeric branch and falls through the switch. It is parsed with `parseInt(decimal, 10)` to 39 and converted with `String.fromCharCode`, giving `'`.
answers.q4: Code points above 0x10FFFF and surrogate code points 0xD800–0xDFFF are left untouched. The original entity text is returned unchanged.
answers.q5: It subtracts 0x10000 from the code point and builds a surrogate pair with `String.fromCharCode(0xD800 + (cp >> 10), 0xDC00 + (cp & 0x3FF))`. So `😀` becomes `\uD83D\uDE00`.
answers.q6: It asserts that `unescape('&lt; &#60; &quot;')` returns `'< < "'`, so only one layer of decoding happens per call.
answers.q7: The string `© '   &unknown; & < &constructor; &toString;` must stay unchanged. A second assertion requires `&unknown;&©` to become `&unknown;&©`.
answers.q8: `npm test` failed with exit code 127 and the message `sh: 1: mocha: not found`, because the script runs `mocha test/` and Mocha isn't installed.
answers.q9: Mocha was missing, so the agent shimmed `describe` and `it` onto `node:test` globals to run the existing `test/index.js`. It exited 0 with 30 tests, 30 passing, 0 failing.
answers.q10: One. A single apply_patch edited test/unescape.test.js, index.js and README.md, and `node --test test/unescape.test.js` then passed on the first run with exit 0.

q1.why: Exact regex and name matchEntityRegExp given, with semicolon and global flag.

q2.why: unescapeHtml and module.exports.unescape = unescapeHtml; default stays escapeHtml.

q3.why: Numeric decimal branch, parseInt gives 39, fromCharCode yields apostrophe.

q4.why: Both >0x10FFFF and surrogates D800-DFFF; original text returned.

q5.why: Manual surrogate pair via subtract 0x10000 and fromCharCode math.

q7.why: Full string matches key including apos, copy, nbsp, AMP, LT, constructor, toString.
